items.check: Every added baseline case's recorded stdout is free of OS-dependent text; specifically no `csv_written=`/`output_written=` line renders a Path with the host separator

The 4 new --csv cases and 3 new writing cases print `csv_written={Path}` / `output_written={Path}` (reconnect_cmd.py:85, rewrite.py write_nml_safely); confirm the plan states the manifest is Windows-locked or adds a normalisation
Constraint 'Every added case is deterministic across runs, machines and temp directories' is falsifiable against the existing manifest entry `csv_written=out\inspect.csv`
DL-014's stated reason for normalising the ambiguous-writing case ('the ambiguity CSV records candidate paths') matches _write_ambiguity_csv's actual row shape {artist,title,old_path,reason}
AC requires exactly two normalise_run_root entries; verify the ambiguous-writing case's recorded bytes actually contain the run root, else the relaxation is unjustified
PARITY_BASELINE_SHA256 ships as "0"*64; no intent or code_change fills it, yet M-002 AC requires the guard to pass

test_normalised_case_still_detects_a_non_run_root_byte_change asserts only `written != corrupted`; it passes vacuously if normalisation masks everything. R-005 is recorded as mitigated by a test that cannot detect the risk

Stacked diffs against the same file carry hunk headers computed from the ORIGINAL file, so applying CC-M-001-004 then -005 then -006 then -009 then -011 to regenerate.py will not land at the stated offsets; declared hunk line counts also disagree with body line counts
AC requires tests/baselines/CLAUDE.md to 'record that SHA beside it' (the tag's commit SHA); CC-M-003-006's diff records no SHA, and the SHA is unknowable before the commit exists
manifest.json is CRLF on disk with no .gitattributes and no repo-wide core.autocrlf pin; a SHA-256 byte pin over a text-mode-written file is fragile across clones

_run_root_forms sorts a set by len with ties (native vs forward-slash forms are equal length); set iteration order is hash-randomised, so substitution order varies per process in a module whose purpose is determinism
`next(c for c in manifest if ...)` with no default raises StopIteration rather than failing cleanly when no normalised case exists
rewrite-from-reconnect output is argv[2] (verified: register() adds old_input then output); _output_paths' existing --csv branch already captures the CSV separately
size="16" matches diskscan's filesize=str(file_stat.st_size) for the 16-zero-byte stub, and --match-confidence filename admits the filename_size tier
parse_volume_map keys on str(Path(scan_root)) and resolve_volume_identity looks up str(Path(scan_root)); relative 'recon/audio' normalises identically on both sides
index_scan_roots is called with stats=None so its files_seen/cache_hits counters are discarded and never reach stdout
diskscan.py line 103 is `for path in sorted(Path(root).rglob("*")):`
recon/ as a sibling of corpus/ leaves the scan-compare-candidates case (which scans corpus only) byte-identical
No code_change touches a file under traktor_nml/; scope constraint honoured
